sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 8 Status
sections.summary: Devnet 8 is live and approaching Gloas fork transition in ~2 days 17 hours; devnet 7 will be sunset after the transition.
sections.body:
- A [blog post](https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/08/17/plataberget-testnet) and [tweet](https://x.com/ethPandaOps/status/2089333243946377624) were published announcing devnet 8.
- Devnet 7 will be sunset once devnet 8 completes the Gloas transition.
- Nimbus reported that if [consensus-specs PR #5543](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5543) lands quickly enough across CL clients, devnet 8 should be fine, as the change is consensus-breaking.
- Builder deposits should be submitted a few epochs before the fork epoch; a builder deposits view is available on [Dora](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/builders/deposits).
- Testing focuses are documented in the [devnet 8 notes](https://notes.ethereum.org/@ethpandaops/glamsterdam-devnet-8); SSZ testing will be deferred to later T-NETs.
- The validator set is smaller than devnet 7 because exited validators were not added this time.
- Different client teams are encouraged to notify EthPandaOps about builder software they want tested.
- Fallback clients are also on the testing list.

sections.heading: Contributor Program Registration
sections.summary: Ahmad Wilson asked about re-enrolling in the contributor program after the Batsu-to-computer transition; EthPandaOps will follow up after vacation.
sections.body:
- Ahmad Wilson noted that the previous contributor registration system (Batsu) appears deprecated and asked how to re-enroll.
- Parithosh Jayanthi (EthPandaOps) said several team members were on vacation the past week and a half; Andrew or Sam will look at the request shortly.

sections.heading: EIP-7610 Removal from Glamsterdam
sections.summary: Consensus reached to remove EIP-7610 from Glamsterdam since the edge case it guards is infeasible without breaking Ethereum's hash-collision security model; EIP-8253 nonce bump proposed for Hegota instead.
sections.body:
- [EIP-7610](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7610) requires checking storage-root emptiness before contract deployment to protect ~28 accounts with non-empty storage eligible for deployment via hash collision.
- Gary argued the attack requires a hash collision (160-bit security), which would also allow deriving private keys for arbitrary addresses — a far larger break of Ethereum security — making the check unnecessary.
- Dragan (Reth) supported removal, noting Reth already skips the EIP-7610 tests and receives recurring complaints from auditors/researchers about failing them; he described it as a recurring nuisance.
  - Reth does not check the storage route; behavior under these tests is undefined and client-dependent.
- Geth also currently skips the EIP-7610 tests due to hard-coded address handling.
- Jochem-brouwer agreed, citing the expensive disk-level storage-root check the EIP's spec surface implies, and the testing friction it causes.
- [EIP-8253](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8253) was proposed for inclusion in Hegota instead; it bumps the nonce for only the specific 28 mainnet accounts, eliminating the edge case permanently.
  - EIP-8253 avoids the general-purpose testing problem because it targets only the known accounts, not a general scenario.
- Karim T. (Nethermind) noted that for PBT (Portal Bridge Tree) there will be no storage root, making EIP-7610's check impossible in that context as well.
- Kevaundray Wedderburn confirmed bumping the nonce in Hegota makes sense and asked whether it was not in Glamsterdam simply because it was never CFI'd for it; Dragan affirmed the priority is shipping Glamsterdam quickly.
- Jochem-brouwer will raise the removal at the next ACDC call for formal decision.
  - Spencer asked whether this could be raised at ACDC this week to keep turnaround under a week.
  - Jochem-brouwer confirmed he will place it at ACDC and reference this conversation.
- Removing EIP-7610 means the related tests will be removed from EVM spec tests, allowing Geth, Reth, and other clients to pass the canonical test suite without skipping.
